newsitem.title: CROATIA: Bosnian alumina maker hopes to restart production.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian alumina maker hopes to restart production.

text.p: Bosnian alumina factory Aluminij hopes to restart production in 1997 with the help of foreign investments, after being shut down for five years due to war.
"Foreign capital is here now and we do not lack knowledge," director Mijo Brajkovic was quoted as saying by Croatian daily Vjesnik.
The paper said Aluminij, situated in Mostar in southern Bosnia, signed deals worth $30 million with the American firm Venco and CTI of Venezuela this week.
CTI is to provide technical help in renewing Aluminij's production lines by February next year to enable exports of electrodes by the Bosnian firm to carbon manufacturer Venco.
But it was not clear how much money would be invested in rebuilding its facilities, destroyed by the former Yugoslav Army and Serb shelling in spring 1992, or who would provide it.
The company could not be reached for comment.

Vjesnik said it used to be Bosnia's leading exporter when the war-torn republic was still a part of Yugoslavia. It was the only producer of alumina for the country's metal processors. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
